metadata.note: San Jose's electric street railways, 1890-1938. Two rival systems: the San Jose & Santa Clara Railway (horse 1868, electric 1890; San Jose & Santa Clara County Railway from 1905) on Santa Clara Street and The Alameda, which absorbed the Alum Rock Railway in 1905; and the People's Horse Railroad group (First Street Railroad, Market Street & Willow Glen) on First Street, which became the San Jose Railroad Company in 1894. Southern Pacific interests controlled both by 1909 and merged them in 1912 as San Jose Railroads, which took over the Peninsular Railway's San Jose city lines in 1933, converted most routes to buses under the 1934-35 resettlement franchise and ran its last streetcars on 10 April 1938. National City Lines bought the bus company in 1939 (San Jose City Lines). Horse years are excluded (Rule 5): every feature starts at electrification or at its first steam-dummy run.
metadata.colour_note: Three operators, colours pre-assigned by the Bay Area batch coordinator: San Jose Railroads #D4762C (including its own predecessors the People's Horse Railroad and the San Jose Railroad Company - one continuously operating company that renamed in 1894 and absorbed the SJ&SC in 1912); San Jose and Santa Clara Railway #E0A458 (including its 1905 reorganization as the San Jose & Santa Clara County Railway); Alum Rock Railway #A6582B.
metadata.ownership_note: Rule 4 splits are at the 1905 Alum Rock Railway takeover and the 1912 SJ&SC merger, the dates the company running the cars changed. Southern Pacific's acquisition of control (by 1909) is NOT a split: both companies kept operating under their own names until 1912, and Southern Pacific never ran the city cars itself. The four Peninsular-built city lines (Seventeenth Street, Bascom, Park Avenue, Naglee) are drawn only from the 1933 takeover; their Peninsular years belong to the Peninsular Railway layer.
metadata.mode_note: Santa Clara line is interurban (Rule 7: built to join two separate towns); everything else is streetcar, including the Alum Rock park line (city to a park, not between communities) and Willow Glen (a city line into an adjoining suburb).
source: McCaleb, Charles S. Tracks, Tires and Wires (Interurban Press, 1981) - cited by Wikipedia, not consulted
metadata.geometry_quality: Street-running throughout: no San Jose streetcar track survives. The Santa Clara line west of 17th Street is the OpenHistoricalMap trace (CC0, relations 2749985-2749988; geometry only, never dates); every other line is routed with a staged shortest path over today's OpenStreetMap road grid along the streets the sources name. Straight-line legs: 0.37 mi (Hobson Street, severed by SR 87) and 0.28 mi (Delmas Avenue, cut by I-280). Approximate legs: 1.0 mi Kirk Avenue - Penitencia Creek (Alum Rock line, 1896-1911) and ~2 mi east of Noble Avenue into Alum Rock Park (1923-32), both private right of way now gone. Each feature's geometry_quality gives its traced length.
metadata.peninsular_note: The Peninsular Railway interurbans to Los Gatos, Saratoga, Campbell, Cupertino, Palo Alto and Berryessa ran on San Jose streets, partly on San Jose Railroads track (Willow Street, Delmas Avenue in 1922; the King Road/Berryessa park line was Peninsular track worked by San Jose Railroads cars). They are not drawn here; see the Peninsular Railway layer.

segments.note: San Jose & Santa Clara Railway, overhead-trolley electric line from East San Jose along Santa Clara Street and The Alameda to Santa Clara. The horse railroad of 1868 had tried Frank Fisher's underground-conduit electric system from 4 September 1888, but History San Jose records that it failed so often that service was suspended and the HORSECARS RETURNED; the conduit was replaced by overhead wire in 1889, and the reincorporated San Jose & Santa Clara Railway (October 1889) opened as an electric line in 1890. Drawn from 1890, not 1888, so that no drawn year covers horse haulage (Rule 5). headway_min is an ESTIMATE - no San Jose streetcar timetable for these years was found. Mode is interurban under Rule 7: the line was built (horsecar 1868, electric 1888-90) to link two separate towns, San Jose and Santa Clara, three miles apart across open country along The Alameda - the same case as Dunkirk - Fredonia. By the 1930s The Alameda was built up end to end, but the test is what the line was for.
sources: Segment-level: electric opening 1890 from chicagorailfan's route table and santacruztrains (incorporated Oct 1889, opened 1890); the 1888 Fisher trial and the return of horses from History San Jose and Electrical World. CONFLICT: Wikipedia (The Alameda) says the line "reopened in 1888" electric and was converted to overhead in 1889 - recorded, not followed, because of the horsecar return.

segments.note: Reorganized in 1905 as the San Jose & Santa Clara County Railway, which also absorbed the Alum Rock Railway that year. (santacruztrains says the SJ&SC was consolidated into the Peninsular Railroad on 30 June 1909; chicagorailfan and Wikipedia both have it merging into San Jose Railroads in 1912 - CONFLICT recorded; this file follows the 1912 merger.) headway_min is an ESTIMATE - no San Jose streetcar timetable for these years was found.
sources: Segment-level: 1905 reorganization and 1912 merger from chicagorailfan's company history; SP control by 1909 from chicagorailfan.

properties.line: San Jose Railroads: Alum Rock Park (via King Road)

properties.geometry_quality: Traced 7.13 mi. Drawn from Alum Rock Avenue at King Road; the cars reached King Road over the Linda Vista line. Routed on the OSM road grid along King Road, Berryessa Road and Penitencia Creek Road into the park; 0.43 mi of the route (near Lundy Avenue at King/Berryessa, and Summerdale Drive between Berryessa Road and Penitencia Creek Road) runs off the named streets. segments.note: In 1932 the Railroad Commission recorded that San Jose Railroads ran the passenger cars to Alum Rock Park "from Santa Clara Avenue to King Road, thence along King Road to Berryessa Road and from this point on private right of way into the Park" - the track beyond Santa Clara Avenue belonged to the Peninsular Railway, which ran freight on it. Passenger service east of Berryessa was authorized to end by the order of 28 March 1932 (6,671 riders in five months); Wikipedia gives the last park car as 11 July 1932. The 1923 start is chicagorailfan's date for the King Road line. Before 1923 (from 2 September 1913) park cars ran up Berryessa Road from a connection on 17th Street, over the Peninsular's line - not drawn here; see the Peninsular Railway layer. headway_min is an ESTIMATE - no San Jose streetcar timetable for these years was found.
sources: Segment-level: route, ownership and operator from CPUC Decision 24622 (1932); end date from Wikipedia (Alum Rock Park); the 1923 start is chicagorailfan's King Road date and is NOT confirmed as the date San Jose Railroads cars began using it.

segments.note: Delmas Avenue line, built by the Market Street & Willow Glen Railroad (horsecars from 1877; controlled by the People's Horse Railroad from 1882) and electrified in 1892. After May 1921 one route ran on Delmas, San Fernando and Julian Streets. Peninsular Railway through cars to Los Gatos via Campbell were rerouted over Willow Street and Delmas in 1922. Delmas Avenue south of San Carlos went to buses on 23 February 1935 over residents' protests. headway_min is an ESTIMATE - no San Jose streetcar timetable for these years was found.
